react_result.final_narrative_text: Across four enrichment paradigms, a six-steroid module dominated the differential signal. MetaboAnalystR PSEA (KEGG) ranked KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) as the sole significant hit (p = 5.77e-07, 6/87 pathway metabolites). RaMP ORA independently nominated the equivalent SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' pathway with extraordinary significance (FDR = 4.97e-18, fold-enrichment 1501×, 6/27 hits). Mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis placed 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) as the top-ranked pathway (p = 8.4e-05, 14/14 network-compound overlap) and independently captured 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde in a secondary tyrosine metabolism hit (p = 0.024). The six shared driver steroids — 17β-estradiol, androstenedione, estrone, dehydroepiandrosterone, dihydrotestosterone, and testosterone — are canonical intermediates of the steroidogenic cascade from pregnenolone through sex hormones, consistent with CYP17A1, HSD3B, and aromatase (CYP19A1) catalytic roles. Warfarin did not map to any steroid pathway in any paradigm, suggesting an independent pharmacological action (vitamin K antagonism) unlinked to sex-steroid metabolism in this dataset.

RaMP additionally nominated the Reactome analogue R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones, FDR = 4.38e-17) and WikiPathways WP:WP496 (Steroid biosynthesis) among the top ten. MetaboAnalystR PSEA (KEGG) ranked KEGG:hsa00140 (Steroid hormone biosynthesis) as the sole significant hit (p = 5.77e-07, 6/87 pathway metabolites). RaMP ORA independently nominated the equivalent SMPDB:SMP00068 / KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' pathway with extraordinary significance (FDR = 4.97e-18, fold-enrichment 1501×, 6/27 hits). Mummichog's m/z-direct network analysis placed 'Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism' (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) as the top-ranked pathway (p = 8.4e-05, 14/14 network-compound overlap) and independently captured 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde in a secondary tyrosine metabolism hit (p = 0.024).
